name: database
description: Read-only connector for a deployment's own database, for troubleshooting and support: licenses/subscriptions, moderation surfaces (tickets/knowledge/mail), instance health.

listing.summary: Read-only access to your deployment's own database for troubleshooting and support.

setupGuide.summary: Connect either a direct Postgres DSN (same machine/network, or a hardened public endpoint) OR a liaison-db-gate URL+token (recommended for cross-network / grumpy-devops setups). Exactly one mode — never both.

steps.text: Rung 0/1 (same machine or private network): mint a read-only role with `scripts/db-readonly-role.ts --create` and paste its DSN into connectionString.

Rung 2 (db-gate, recommended for anything crossing an untrusted network): stand up the liaison/db-gate sidecar next to your database with a catalog.yaml and a minted bearer token, then paste its URL into gateUrl and the token into gateToken.
Rung 3 (public Postgres endpoint): connectionString with TLS required — the connector refuses plaintext to any non-local resolved IP.
After connecting, db_probe runs automatically and reports any write/EXECUTE grants beyond the read-only allow-list — review its warnings before relying on this connection.

credentialFields.name: connectionString
credentialFields.label: Postgres or Redshift DSN for a read-only role (direct mode only)

credentialFields.name: statementTimeoutMs
credentialFields.label: Statement timeout in ms, 1000 to 300000 (default 10000). Agent tool calls cap it at 55000

setupGuide.summary: A second, direct-only database connection for raw read-only SELECT (an analytics warehouse or a replica). Agents target it with db_query / db_describe / db_probe connection: "warehouse". The default connection is untouched.

steps.text: Create a role that holds only USAGE + SELECT on the schemas agents may read.
Paste its DSN into connectionString (TLS is required for any public-resolving host: add sslmode=require).
Set dialect to redshift for Amazon Redshift; leave it empty for Postgres.
Grant database:query:read only to the roles or agents that should use it: every tool call on the warehouse (describe and probe included) requires that scope.

db_list_reads.description: List the named, curated reads this database connector's catalog offers — call this first to discover what's available.

db_read.description: Run a named, parameterized curated read from the catalog (see db_list_reads). Column output is restricted to the read's declared allow-list.

db_describe.description: List the tables the connected role can SELECT (name and column count), or describe one table's columns and types (secret columns filtered out). connection "warehouse" requires database:query:read.

table.description: schema.table: returns that table's columns and types. Omit to list tables without their columns

schema.description: Without table: list only this schema's tables

search.description: Without table: list only tables whose schema.table contains this text (case-insensitive)

connection.description: Which connection to use: "default" (the org's database connection, the default) or "warehouse" (the second, direct connection, when configured)

db_probe.description: Run the connect-time safety probe on demand: reports unexpected write grants, dangerous EXECUTE grants, and catalog drift (gate mode). connection "warehouse" requires database:query:read.

connection.description: Which connection to use: "default" (the org's database connection, the default) or "warehouse" (the second, direct connection, when configured)

db_query.description: Run a raw, single-statement, SELECT-only SQL query against the connected database. Enabled by default; a deployment can disable it with LIAISON_DATABASE_ALLOW_RAW_QUERY=false. Same read-only role/grant restrictions as curated reads: nothing outside the allow-list is visible.

sql.description: A single SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) statement, at most 100000 characters

connection.description: Which connection to use: "default" (the org's database connection, the default) or "warehouse" (the second, direct connection, when configured)

report_access_get.description: The Report access settings: each domain of the connected catalog with its reads, the catalog default, the organization rule, and the roles and people a rule can name.

report_access_set.description: Replace the organization's Report access rules (one map of domain to tier, roles and people).

domainAccess.description: Domain to rule: { tier: internal|confidential|restricted, roles?: role ids, users?: user ids }

report_access_find_people.description: Find people of the organization by email, for naming them in a Report access rule.

member.description: Database connector reader: curated reads only

agentInstructions:
Read-only access to a connected SQL database for troubleshooting and answering questions. The SCHEMA is DEPLOYMENT-SPECIFIC — do NOT assume any table or column names exist (there is no generic "licenses", "organizations", or "orders" table unless discovery shows one). Discover first, then query:
1. db_describe() with NO argument lists every table you can actually read (schema.table and its column count; narrow with schema or search). db_describe(table: "schema.table") returns that table's columns and types. Secret/credential columns are excluded by the database role, so anything it lists is safe to select. ALWAYS start here to learn the real shape before answering.
2. db_query(sql) runs any read-only SELECT — this is the primary tool for real questions (lookups, filters, joins, aggregates, "latest N"). Base your SQL on what db_describe returned. Only a single-statement SELECT/WITH is allowed; writes, DDL, multiple statements, and dangerous functions are rejected. A query that runs past the time limit is cancelled on the database and returns statement_timeout: do not rerun it unchanged, narrow it (filter by hub and date range, aggregate) first. Example shape: SELECT <cols> FROM <schema.table> WHERE <...> ORDER BY <...> LIMIT <n>.
3. db_list_reads() / db_read(name, params) expose CURATED named reads IF this deployment shipped an adapter with them. They may be absent or may not match this database — if db_list_reads is empty or a db_read errors, ignore it and use db_describe + db_query.

Everything is strictly read-only and safe by construction: writes are impossible, and secret/credential columns (tokens, password hashes, signed licenses, API secrets) are not granted — selecting one returns a permission error rather than data, which simply means that column is off-limits; pick the readable columns db_describe showed you. If the database is not connected, surface the not_connected error — never fabricate data. Ground every answer in db_describe + a real db_query; do not guess at schema.

Some deployments configure a second connection, "warehouse" (an analytics warehouse or a replica). db_describe, db_query and db_probe take an optional connection param: omit it for the default database, pass connection: "warehouse" to target the warehouse. Describe the warehouse with db_describe(connection: "warehouse") before querying it; curated reads (db_list_reads / db_read) exist only on the default connection.
